descriptionChirho: Physical stretching out of the hand or arm, often in divine action or human gesture (Arabic madda/مَدَّ); includes imperative, consecutive imperfect, perfect, infinitive, and conjunctive perfect forms in Qal active voice.

Passive participle describing the state of being stretched out, characteristically used of God's outstretched arm (Arabic mamduda/مَمْدُودَة); includes both feminine and masculine forms, with and without article.
Active participle describing the one who stretches out or spreads (heavens, tent curtains), often of God as cosmic creator (Arabic nashara/نَشَرَ or basata/بَسَطَ); Qal participial forms.
Qal finite forms meaning to spread out, extend, or stretch physically (wings, heavens); overlaps with stretch-out sense but context is cosmic or territorial spreading (Arabic nashara/بَسَطَ).
Stretching out or setting up a tent or tabernacle (Arabic nasaba/نَصَبَ); a specialized concrete application of the root in Qal.
Intransitive turning aside from a path, road, or moral standard (Arabic mala/مَالَ); Qal perfect, imperfect, imperative, infinitive, and participle forms expressing self-directed deviation.

Intransitive inclining, bowing, or leaning physically — of shadows declining, terrain sloping, or a person bowing (Arabic mala/مَالَ or inhidara/اِنْحَدَرَ); Qal forms where the subject itself inclines.

Hifil causative meaning to incline or direct one's ear or heart toward God or instruction (Arabic amala/أَمَالَ or amil/أَمِلْ); includes imperative, imperfect, perfect, and infinitive Hifil forms used in prayer and exhortation.
Hifil causative meaning to turn someone or something aside, to lead astray, to divert from a path (Arabic amala with object/حَوَّلَ); includes turning aside persons, causing deviation.
Hifil forms specifically meaning to pervert, distort, or twist justice or judgment (Arabic harrafa/حَرَّفَ); a morally charged specialization of the causative turn-aside sense.
